sources.citation: OLAC. 2025. OLAC resources in and about the Yau language [yyu] (combined catalog, up-to-date 23 Jan 2025). http://www.language-archives.org/language/yyu
sources.note: Bibliographic check only (Wayback copy; live site unreachable). Lists six resources: Rosetta Project Swadesh list, transnewguinea.org, Glottolog, PARADISEC DL2-002 (Laycock Notebook C2), Ethnologue, LINGUIST List. No grammar, sketch or phonology of Yau in any OLAC archive.

sources.citation: Greenhill, Simon J. (ed.). 2025. transnewguinea.org: Yau [yaus1235] lexicon, 46 items, source Laycock (1968). https://transnewguinea.org/language/yau; and The Rosetta Project. 2010. Yau Swadesh List (archive.org rosettaproject_yyu_swadesh-1)
sources.note: Nothing. Wordlist forms carry vowel-length marks (ru:neʔ 'bad', pi:ren 'dog', nu:lai 'moon') but no stress marks; both lists derive from Laycock 1968.

sources.citation: Eberhard, Simons & Fennig (eds.). 2019. Ethnologue, 22nd ed., entry 'Yau' [yyu]. SIL International. https://www.ethnologue.com/language/yyu
sources.note: Nothing. 'Population 200 (2014 SIL)... Sandaun province: northwest of Lumi, Senim village... Dialects: None known. Lexical similarity: 63% with Olo [ong] and Yis [yis]... Different from Yau [yuw] and Yawu dialect of Yessan-Mayo [yss].' (Wayback copy of the open 2019 page.)

sources.citation: SIL PNG. 2013. PNG Language Resources: 'Yau information' [yyu] and 'PNG Bibliography by language, Y'. http://www-01.sil.org/pacific/png/
sources.note: Nothing. Yau [yyu] page: 'Language resources: Nothing yet available or materials are not yet processed.' The letter-Y bibliography index lists Yau [yuw] (Morobe) but no Yau [yyu] entries (Wayback copies).

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1975. The Torricelli Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 767-780. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone. p. 769: 'Phonologically, the languages are characterised by the following statements: three positions of articulation; usually no voicing contrast in consonant phonemes; five to eight vowels...; fairly high proportion of fricative consonants'; the phoneme example is Olo, not Yau. Yau appears only as a Wapei-family member with 140 speakers (Jan 1970, p. 773) and in the note 'Yau-Yis (71%)' lexical sharing (p. 768).

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. 1973. Sepik languages: checklist and preliminary classification. Pacific Linguistics B-25. Canberra: ANU. iv+129 pp. hdl:1885/146478 (ANU Open Research, open access)
sources.note: Nothing. Yau is entry 17 (printed p. 9): 'Village: Seinam [CD32W]. Comments: Test DCL67 (John Pilem, Clemen Engiape/Seinam); see Laycock (1968:6).' The Torricelli Phylum introduction (p. 7) says only that the phonology 'differs from that of most other Sepik groups in permitting vowel sequences, and in having a large (5 to 8) number of vowel phonemes.' No occurrence of 'stress' or 'accent' in the volume's text layer.

sources.citation: Wikipedia. 'Yau language (Torricelli)'; Wikidata Q8050328; ISO 639-3 record yyu; ANU Open Research API searches 'Yau Wapei' and 'Lumi Subdistrict Laycock'
sources.note: Nothing; Wikipedia has no phonology section (200 speakers, 2014; Senim village). ANU repository searches return no Yau-specific item (hits: Laycock 1973, Scorza 1985 Au, McGregor & McGregor 1982 Olo, Feldman Awtuw).
